newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to send 1997 budget to Congress tonight.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to send 1997 budget to Congress tonight.

text.p: Argentina's government will send to Congress Friday its 1997 budget which anticipates growth of five percent and a $3 billion budget deficit, government officials said.
The document will be sent to Congress this evening. Together with anticipated debt redemption costs of $9 billion and the deficit of $3 billion, the budget anticipates $12 billion of new debt.

Debt interest payments expected to be $4.5 billion will be covered by tax revenues, which the government anticipates will rise next year compared with 1996, allowing it to keep its promise of reducing value added tax to 20 percent from 21 percent.

Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said this week the lowering of value-added tax depends on tax revenues in the first quarter. The government is expecting that the proposed tax hikes on fuel and a pick-up in economic growth will generate higher revenues.
Fernandez has promised government spending will remain at the same level in 1997 as this year, at $41 billion.
